responses.content: {"summary": "The source argues that local AI agents let small businesses keep proprietary data on their own hardware and run routine drafting and classification on a 12 GB consumer GPU without per-token fees, while conceding that frontier models still lead at long multi-step reasoning.", "claims": [{"claim": "Local AI agents keep proprietary data on the machine instead of a cloud.", "label": "SOURCE_STATED", "source_excerpt": "Local AI agents keep proprietary data on the machine"}, {"claim": "A 9B-parameter model is practical on a consumer GPU with 12 GB of VRAM.", "label": "SOURCE_STATED", "source_excerpt": "Running a 9B-parameter model on a consumer GPU with 12 GB of VRAM is now practical"}, {"claim": "Running routine work such as ticket summaries locally avoids per-token fees.", "label": "SOURCE_STATED", "source_excerpt": "avoids per-token cloud fees"}, {"claim": "Local models are weaker than frontier models at long, multi-step reasoning.", "label": "SOURCE_STATED", "source_excerpt": "Local models are still weaker than frontier models at long, multi-step reasoning"}, {"claim": "Switching to local AI cuts a small business's AI costs by 80%.", "label": "SOURCE_STATED", "source_excerpt": "cuts AI costs by 80%"}, {"claim": "Most small teams will run a hybrid local/cloud setup within two years.", "label": "OPINION", "source_excerpt": null}, {"claim": "Cloud LLM API prices keep falling every year.", "label": "NEEDS_VERIFICATION", "source_excerpt": null}], "opposing_perspectives": ["Cloud providers offer contractual data protection that may be enough for most teams.", "Hardware, power and maintenance can outweigh per-token fees at low volumes."], "open_questions": ["What does a local setup cost per month for a five-person team?", "Which everyday tasks are good enough on a 9B model?", "How do you decide what stays local and what goes to the cloud?"]}
